memory_annotations.evidence_summary: No explicit durable preference evidence was introduced; all choices were limited to the schedule and logistics of this wedding trip.

messages.content: I need to start a separate trip for my niece’s wedding in Raleigh. My spouse is coming, so this is for two people. The wedding is Saturday, May 3, and we need to be there for a family dinner Friday evening.

I’ll treat this separately from the Chicago trip. Are you leaving from Denver, and do you want to return Sunday, May 4? I also need the dinner time and the wedding location, since those will determine whether a downtown hotel or one nearer the ceremony works better.

Yes, Denver to Raleigh-Durham and back Sunday. Dinner is at 7:00 Friday in downtown Raleigh. The ceremony is at 4:00 Saturday at a venue near Cary, about twenty minutes from downtown according to my sister.

That makes a Friday arrival by roughly 5:00 p.m. the latest comfortable target, allowing time to collect bags and get from RDU to the hotel before dinner. For Sunday, is there a brunch or other family event, or can the return flight leave at any reasonable time?
There may be brunch downtown from 10:00 to noon. I don’t want to commit to anything that makes us leave in the middle of it.

Then I would look at Sunday departures no earlier than about 3:00 p.m. RDU is usually 20 to 30 minutes from downtown by car, but returning a rental and airport screening argue for leaving the city around 12:45 to 1:00. Do you want me to compare nonstop flights with one-stop options, or focus on schedule first?
Compare both. This is a short trip, so a connection only makes sense if it saves a meaningful amount or fixes the Friday timing.

For a May 2-4 trip, the useful patterns are likely to be: a Friday morning nonstop arriving RDU in the early afternoon, a later nonstop that lands too close to dinner, and one-stop itineraries through Dallas, Atlanta, or Charlotte. The morning nonstop is the cleanest fit. Illustrative round-trip totals for two in regular economy are about $780-$940 nonstop versus $620-$760 with one stop, before bags or seat fees. A connection adds roughly two to three hours each way and increases the risk of missing dinner if the outbound is disrupted.
The morning nonstop sounds better for Friday. What does Sunday look like if we wait until after brunch?

A nonstop leaving RDU around 4:00 to 5:30 p.m. would fit well and reach Denver in the early evening local time. A 3:00 p.m. departure is possible but leaves little margin if brunch runs late. One-stop returns departing around 3:30 may not reach Denver until 8:30 or 9:30 p.m. The best working combination is therefore a Friday morning nonstop and a Sunday late-afternoon nonstop, subject to the live schedule and fare.
Use that as the flight plan for now. We each need a normal carry-on, so include any airline fees that would change the comparison. Now help me decide where to stay.

For one shared room on Friday and Saturday nights, there are three practical approaches. A downtown Raleigh hotel keeps Friday dinner and Sunday brunch easy, with a round-trip rideshare or rental car for the Cary wedding. A Cary hotel simplifies Saturday but adds travel for dinner and brunch. Splitting hotels after one night would reduce one Saturday drive but creates a checkout, luggage, and second check-in on a two-night stay, so it offers little benefit.
Agreed, no split hotel. Can you compare the downtown and Cary versions including transportation?

A downtown room for two nights is roughly $430-$560 including estimated taxes. Airport rideshares plus downtown-to-Cary travel for the ceremony and reception could bring transportation to about $170-$240, depending on late-night demand. A two-day rental is roughly $150-$220 before downtown hotel parking, which may add $60-$90. A Cary room may run about $330-$450 including estimated taxes, with free or lower-cost parking more common; however, you would drive or rideshare downtown Friday, back after dinner, downtown again Sunday, and then to RDU.
The reception is at the same Cary venue and goes until about 10:30. Would getting a rideshare back downtown that late be a problem?

It should generally be possible, but pickup time and surge pricing are less predictable at a private venue, especially when many guests leave together. Ask whether the couple is arranging a shuttle or whether the venue has a designated rideshare pickup area. Without a shuttle, a rental car gives you more control, though one of you would need to remain able to drive after the reception.
My sister just texted that there will be a shuttle from one downtown hotel, the Raleigh Marriott City Center, leaving at 2:45 and returning after the reception. We are not required to stay there.

That materially improves the downtown plan. The Marriott is convenient if its wedding block is still open, but a nearby hotel could work if the walk to the shuttle pickup is manageable in formal clothes. I would compare the Marriott block rate with two nearby options and verify whether non-guests may board the shuttle.

She says non-guests can use it if their names are on the family list. The block at the Marriott is $229 per night before tax. Another option she sent is the Residence Inn about a ten-minute walk away at $189 before tax.

For two nights, the Marriott would likely total about $520-$550 after tax, while the Residence Inn would be about $430-$460. The roughly $90 difference buys direct shuttle access and avoids two walks in wedding clothes, including the late return. Both keep Friday dinner and Sunday brunch convenient. Check whether either rate includes parking and whether the wedding block has a more restrictive cancellation deadline than the public flexible rate.
We probably won’t need a car if the shuttle works. Is airport rideshare plus the downtown hotel the sensible combination, then?

Yes. With the wedding shuttle confirmed, rideshares between RDU and downtown remove the parking and rental-return costs without creating a Saturday transportation gap. Budget roughly $60-$100 total for the two airport rides, with extra margin for demand. The remaining hotel decision is whether direct shuttle pickup is worth about $90 more over the stay.
Let’s use the Marriott block as the working hotel and the nonstop flights you described. I am not ready to book. Give me the complete version I should confirm with my spouse and sister.

Working plan only, with no purchase: two travelers fly nonstop from Denver to Raleigh-Durham on Friday, May 2, using a morning departure that arrives in the early afternoon and leaves ample time for the 7:00 p.m. family dinner downtown. Return Sunday, May 4, on a nonstop departing RDU around 4:00-5:30 p.m., so you can attend brunch through noon. Allow roughly $780-$940 total for regular economy before any carrier-specific bag or seat charges; verify that each fare includes the carry-on allowance you need.

For lodging, use one room at the Raleigh Marriott City Center for May 2-4 under the wedding block, currently quoted at $229 per night before tax. Confirm the final two-night total, room type, deposit, cancellation deadline, and block availability. Your sister should add both names to the family shuttle list. Confirm the 2:45 p.m. Saturday pickup point and the post-reception return procedure.

Use rideshares between RDU and downtown rather than renting a car, with a working round-trip transportation estimate of $60-$100. Before booking anything, verify the live nonstop flight times and total for two, fare restrictions, carry-on terms, the hotel’s itemized total, and that Sunday brunch remains downtown and ends by noon.

updated_continuity_summary: Elena’s solo Chicago conference trip remains unchanged: Southwest nonstop travel March 27-30 and a three-night Central Loop Hotel reservation, with hotel cancellation available through 6:00 p.m. Chicago time on March 26. Separately, Elena and her spouse are planning a Raleigh-area family wedding trip for May 2-4. The working plan is round-trip nonstop travel for two, one shared room for two nights at the Raleigh Marriott City Center under the wedding block, airport rideshares, and use of the family wedding shuttle to the Saturday venue near Cary. Nothing has been purchased. Live flight details and total, fare terms, hotel total and cancellation terms, shuttle-list enrollment, and Sunday brunch details still require confirmation.
